title: 备份恢复
implementation: db.BackupDatabase: WAL checkpoint + atomic cold copy of the SQLite file (0600)
db.EncryptFile/DecryptFile: AES-256-GCM with a random nonce, key loaded from an environment variable via db.LoadKey (64 hex = 32 bytes); wrong keys fail without writing the destination
cmd backup: cold backup with optional encryption; cmd restore: optional decryption + atomic restore with sidecar cleanup
cmd restore-drill: backs up, encrypts, decrypts into a temp directory, opens the restored database, and runs startup consistency - the production database is never touched
snapshots are derived data re-creatable by re-syncing qui; the SQLite backup is the authoritative restore artifact (documented policy, consistent with OBS-03 pruning)

checks.round_trip: PASS: TestBackupAndEncryptedRestoreRoundTrip - plaintext restore drill reads the drill marker; wrong-key decryption fails without output; correct-key decryption restores identical content
checks.key_handling: PASS: TestLoadKeyRejectsBadInput - non-hex and short keys rejected
checks.runtime_drill: PASS: serve created a database, then backup (encrypted, 516124 bytes) and restore-drill reported 32 tables verified from the encrypted backup
checks.upgrade_backup: PASS: db.Upgrade already creates a pre-migration backup and restores it when migration or consistency fails (DB-11 evidence)

scope_note: The drill is a manual/CI command; scheduling it periodically belongs to deployment (cron/systemd) since the server process must not block on drills. Snapshot directory encryption follows the same EncryptFile helper when operators archive the root.
